summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and COPD was admitted for worsening dyspnea and bilateral leg swelling, more pronounced on the right. He was found to have acute anemia (hemoglobin 8.4 g/dL), for which he received one unit of packed red blood cells, and acute kidney injury likely due to cardiorenal syndrome. His dyspnea was multifactorial, attributed to both heart failure exacerbation and COPD exacerbation, and was managed with IV furosemide, oxygen therapy, and a short course of prednisone with azithromycin. Echocardiography confirmed severe aortic stenosis with preserved ejection fraction, and a family meeting decided against invasive intervention due to high procedural risk. The right leg erythema was not infectious or thrombotic and was managed supportively. He improved clinically, with stabilization of renal function, resolution of hypoxemia, and increased exercise tolerance. He was discharged home with home health services, on home oxygen, new respiratory medications, and instructions for weight monitoring and INR follow-up.
